cards.b: The tallest trees (40–50 m+), with umbrella crowns above the canopy.
Dense layer of leaves at 25–40 m that blocks most light; most wildlife lives here.
Pointed leaf ends that let heavy rain run off quickly, preventing fungus.
Large flared roots supporting tall trees on shallow soil.
Nutrients are held in plants; leaf litter decays fast and rain washes nutrients away (leaching).
A plant adapted to very dry conditions.
Thick fleshy stem stores water for long droughts.
Reduce surface area for water loss (transpiration) and deter animals.
Very long roots that reach deep groundwater, e.g. mesquite and acacia.
Logging, cattle ranching, soya/palm oil farming, mining, roads, dams.
Loss of biodiversity, soil erosion, flooding, more CO₂, nutrient loss.

gaps.s: Rainforest trees keep their leaves all year, so they are ___.
The tallest layer of the rainforest is the ___ layer.
Plants adapted to drought are called ___.
Loss of water vapour from leaves is called ___.
Cutting only mature trees is known as ___ logging.
Large flared roots on rainforest trees are ___ roots.
The variety of species in an area is called ___.
Tourism that protects the environment is called ___.

short.q: Describe the structure of the tropical rainforest.
short.model: It has layers: tall emergent trees above a dense canopy, then an understorey of young trees and climbers, and a dark shrub and ground layer where little grows.
points: gives a feature or height for a layer

short.q: Explain how rainforest trees are adapted to the climate.
short.model: Drip tips shed heavy rain quickly. Buttress roots support tall trees on shallow soil, and tall trunks lift leaves toward the light.
points: buttress roots / tall trunks with reason

short.q: Explain how desert plants are adapted to lack of water.
short.model: Cacti store water in stems and have spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss. Others have long tap roots that reach groundwater.
points: storage or reduced leaves with reason
roots (tap or wide shallow) with reason

short.q: Explain two environmental effects of deforestation.
short.model: Soil is eroded because roots no longer bind it, silting rivers. Biodiversity is lost as habitats are destroyed.

short.q: Give two ways deforestation can bring economic benefits.
short.model: Logging and mining create jobs and export income. Cleared land can be used for cattle and soya, giving farmers money.
